# Checker is right, my smoke files were mislabeled: "a b" means b precedes a, so `a,b,c` is wrong and `c,b,a` is right, and the fake cycle line I invented cites an edge that truly isn't there. Re-smoking against real depsort output, then starting the 300-case run in the background.
printf 'a b\nb c\n' > /tmp/p.txt
./depsort /tmp/p.txt > /tmp/real.txt; echo "depsort on a b / b c:"; cat /tmp/real.txt
echo "real output -> [$(awk -v status=0 -f check.awk /tmp/p.txt /tmp/real.txt)]"
printf 'a b\nb c\nc a\nd e\n' > /tmp/cy.txt
./depsort /tmp/cy.txt > /tmp/cy.out; echo "depsort cycle:"; cat /tmp/cy.out
echo "real cycle -> [$(awk -v status=1 -f check.awk /tmp/cy.txt /tmp/cy.out)]"
# cycle line produced for the 3-cycle must be reversed-dependency order; show raw edges
cat /tmp/cy.txt
diff <(./depsort /tmp/t1.txt) <(./depsort < /tmp/t1.txt) && echo "stdin==file OK"

rm -rf cases out
bgrun -n "300-case depsort run" ./run_cases.sh 300</｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter>

Let me verify: pos[b] < pos[a] for edge a->b i.e. b before a. ok.txt: a,b,c: pos[b]=2, pos[a]=1 → 2<1 false → violated. Correct. reversed: pos[b]=2, pos[a]=3 → 2<3 true. Good.

But the fake cycle test: I said "cycle: a b c a" with edges a b, b c. Cycle check uses k = c[i+1] SUBSEP c[i] i.e. edge "b needs a" — that's wrong direction? Cycle line "a b c a" means a needs b, b needs c, c needs a. So for consecutive (c[i], c[i+1]) the dependency is c[i] needs c[i+1], key = c[i] SUBSEP c[i+1]. I wrote c[i+1] SUBSEP c[i]. Hmm but wait — indeg/adj: my depsort's adj[b] contains a. Let me check what depsort actually prints. Earlier: `printf 'a b\nb a\n'` → "cycle: a b a". a needs b, b needs a. consecutive pairs (a,b),(b,a): edge a->b exists, b->a exists. Either key order works for that symmetric case. `printf 'a a'` → "cycle: a a".

For `a b\nb c\nc a` depsort printed "cycle: a c b a". Check: a needs b, b needs c, c needs a. Is "a c" an edge? a needs c? No. So printing a c b a means cycle in reverse-dependency direction: c needs a (yes, edge c->a exists as a c in my key convention a SUBSEP b... hmm).

Let me just define: pair line "x y" = x needs y. depsort adj[y] = x, indeg[x]++. So it's diffing on x. Cycle DFS traverses from x to y? No — findcycle(u) iterates adj[u] = things that need u. So from u it goes to packages that depend on u. Cycle a c b a in that traversal: a → c (c needs a, i.e. line "c a" ✓), c → b (b needs c, line "b c" ✓), b → a (a needs b, line "a b" ✓). Correct.

So for a cycle line "x y z x" produced by depsort, the relationship is: y needs x, z needs y, x needs z. I.e. consecutive (c[i], c[i+1]) means c[i+1] needs c[i], pair line is "c[i+1] c[i]", key c[i+1] SUBSEP c[i]. That's exactly what I wrote: k = c[i+1] SUBSEP c[i]. And the fake test "a b c a" claims b needs a (not present) → correctly flagged as nonexistent edge. So the checker is right and my fake test case was just wrong.

So checker is correct. Good. Let me now double check with real depsort outputs, and rerun the smoke test with proper files. Then start the 300-case run with bgrun.
